1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
3	# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
4	# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
5	# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1
9	
10	# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
11	# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
12	# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
13	#
14	# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
15	# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
16	# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
17	# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
18	# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
19	# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
20	# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
21	#
22	# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
23	# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.
24	
25	# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
26	# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
27	# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
28	zbuild_pg_resolve() {
29	    local _pid="${1:-}"
30	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
31	    local _child _self
32	    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
33	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
34	    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
35	        printf '%s' "$_child"
36	        return 0
37	    fi
38	    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
39	    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
40	    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
41	    #
42	    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
43	    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
44	    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
45	    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
46	    # about.
47	    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
48	        printf '%s' "$_pid"
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
53	# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
54	# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
55	#
56	# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
57	# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
58	# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
59	# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
60	# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
61	_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
62	    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
63	    # as an option.
64	    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
65	    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
66	    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
67	    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
68	        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
69	        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
71	    done
72	    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
73	}
74	
75	# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
76	# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
77	# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
78	_zbuild_pg_grace() {
79	    local _g="${1:-1}"
80	    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
81	}
82	
83	# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
84	#
85	# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
86	# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
87	# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
88	# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
89	# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
90	# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
91	# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
92	#
93	# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
94	# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
95	zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
96	    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
97	    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
98	    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
99	    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
100	    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
101	}
102	
103	# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
104	#
105	# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
106	# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
107	# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
108	# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
109	# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
110	# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
111	#
112	# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
113	# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
114	#
115	# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
116	# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
117	# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
118	# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
119	#
120	# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
121	# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
122	zbuild_pg_register() {
123	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
124	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
125	    local _self
126	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
127	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
128	    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
129	    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
130	    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
131	    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
132	    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
133	    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
134	    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
135	    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
136	    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
137	    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
138	    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
139	    local _start
140	    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
141	    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
142	    return 0
143	}
144	
145	# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
146	zbuild_pg_kill() {
147	    local _pgid="${1:-}"
148	    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
149	    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
150	    local _self
151	    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
152	    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
153	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
154	}
155	
156	# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
157	# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
158	# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
159	zbuild_pid_kill() {
160	    local _pid="${1:-}"
161	    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
162	    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
163	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh — parallel per-platform dispatch (issue #198/#222)
3	# ADR-009: all platforms run concurrently; stage succeeds iff all succeed (rc=2 = partial).
4	# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_FANOUT_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_FANOUT}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_run_fanout ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Usage: _strategy_run_fanout <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
15	#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated (no orch_spawn called here)
16	#   stage      — stage name (e.g. "intake")
17	#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
18	#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
19	#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
20	#
21	# Dispatches one work unit per role×platform pair in parallel via orch_dispatch.
22	# Collects all results with orch_collect.
23	# Calls orch_shutdown and cleans up work units on both success and failure paths.
24	#
25	# Returns:
26	#   0 — all succeeded
27	#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
28	#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
29	#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
30	_strategy_run_fanout() {
31	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
32	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
33	    # | infra_failed | failed.
34	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
35	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
36	    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
37	    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()
38	
39	    local role platform plugin_dir wu
40	    while IFS= read -r role; do
41	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
42	        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
43	            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
44	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
45	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
46	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
47	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
48	            any_plugin_found=true
49	
50	            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
51	                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
52	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
53	                continue
54	            }
55	            work_units+=("$wu")
56	
57	            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
58	                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
59	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
60	                continue
61	            }
62	            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
63	            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
64	        done
65	    done <<< "$roles_out"
66	
67	    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
68	        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
69	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
70	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
71	        return 1
72	    fi
73	
74	    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
75	    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.
76	    if [[ "$dispatch_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
77	        local collect_rc=0
78	        _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
79	        orch_collect "$pool_id" || collect_rc=$?
80	
81	        # orch_collect: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, partial named on
82	        # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME (#1850 — it was rc 2).
83	        if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
84	            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
85	            # #1906: no artifact check here. Each work unit calls plugin_hook_call
86	            # (strategies/common.sh), so scan_plugin_outputs has already enforced
87	            # every declared output for every dispatched plugin.
88	        elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
89	            success_count=$((success_count + 1))
90	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
91	        else
92	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
93	        fi
94	    fi
95	
96	    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
97	    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
98	
99	    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
100	    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
101	    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
102	    fi
103	}
104	
105	# ─── _strategy_cleanup_work_units ────────────────────────────────────────────
106	_strategy_cleanup_work_units() {
107	    [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && return 0
108	    rm -f "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
109	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh — data-driven map over any declared list dimension (issue #1285)
3	# ADR-047: generalizes fanout (platforms) to arbitrary declared dimensions.
4	# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_MAP_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_MAP}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_dimension ─────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Resolves the iteration list for the given dimension name.
15	# For "platforms": uses _DETECTED_PLATFORMS (set by runner before dispatch).
16	# For other names: uses _MAP_DIM_<name> array if set; otherwise empty.
17	# Prints one element per line; no output = empty dimension.
18	_strategy_map_resolve_dimension() {
19	    local dim="${1:-platforms}"
20	    if [[ "$dim" == "platforms" ]]; then
21	        local p
22	        for p in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]+"${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"}"; do
23	            [[ -n "$p" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$p"
24	        done
25	        return 0
26	    fi
27	    # Arbitrary dimension: caller must export _MAP_DIM_<name> as an array.
28	    # Validate dimension name to prevent variable-name injection.
29	    if [[ ! "$dim" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,64}$ ]]; then
30	        warn "map: invalid dimension name: ${dim}" || true
31	        return 1
32	    fi
33	    # Read the caller's _MAP_DIM_<name> array by reference (Bash 5+ floor — see
34	    # scripts/lib/compat.sh). The name was validated above, guarding the target.
35	    # The array lives in the caller's scope (same sourced shell). Guarded
36	    # expansion tolerates an unset target under the caller's `set -u`.
37	    local -n _ref="_MAP_DIM_${dim}"
38	    local elem
39	    for elem in "${_ref[@]+"${_ref[@]}"}"; do
40	        [[ -n "$elem" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$elem"
41	    done
42	}
43	
44	# ─── _strategy_map_resolve_max ───────────────────────────────────────────────
45	# Resolves the max_parallel concurrency cap for a map group.
46	# Input: raw max value from template (_TPL_MAP_MAX_<gid>), e.g. "4", "auto", "".
47	# Mirrors _parallel_resolve_max (parallel-orchestrator.sh) EXACTLY so map and
48	# parallel groups agree on the cap and its fail-safe:
49	#   - explicit positive integer  → used as-is (then capped at _PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP)
50	#   - "auto" / empty             → ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS env override, else CPU count
51	#   - ANYTHING else (non-numeric typo, "0", negative) → CLAMPED TO 1 (fail-safe).
52	# #1312 (Copilot): an invalid template value must NOT silently remove the cap by
53	# falling through to CPU-count concurrency — that is the opposite of safe. Clamp to 1.
54	_strategy_map_resolve_max() {
55	    local raw="${1:-}"
56	    # #1312 (Copilot): reuse the parallel path's readonly cap so map and parallel
57	    # stay in sync if it ever changes — don't duplicate the literal. Falls back to 8
58	    # only when map.sh is sourced standalone (unit tests) without the parallel module.
59	    local cap="${_PARALLEL_MAX_JOBS_CAP:-8}"
60	    local max="$raw"
61	    # "auto" is an explicit request for the CPU-based default (map-specific alias);
62	    # normalise it to empty so the empty-branch resolves the default.
63	    [[ "$max" == "auto" ]] && max=""
64	    if [[ -z "$max" ]]; then
65	        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
66	            max="$ZBUILD_PARALLEL_JOBS"
67	        else
68	            max="$( { nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null; } | head -1 )"  # sigpipe-ok: writer emits exactly one line
69	            [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=4
70	        fi
71	    fi
72	    # Fail-safe clamp: any non-positive-integer (typo, "0", negative) → 1.
73	    [[ "$max" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || max=1
74	    (( max > cap )) && max=$cap
75	    printf '%s' "$max"
76	}
77	
78	# ─── _strategy_run_map ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
79	# Usage: _strategy_run_map <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root> \
80	#                          [dimension] [env_target] [max_parallel] [on_member_error]
81	#   pool_id          — caller-supplied, already validated. Used as the base for
82	#                      per-batch sub-pool ids ("<base>-b<N>", truncated to fit the
83	#                      64-char backend limit). The FIFO-batch loop below spawns and
84	#                      shuts down one sub-pool per batch via orch_spawn/orch_shutdown;
85	#                      the caller's own pool_id is also orch_shutdown at the end.
86	#   stage            — stage name (e.g. "intake")
87	#   roles_out        — newline-delimited list of role names
88	#   state_file       — path to pipeline state file
89	#   plugins_root     — path to plugins directory
90	#   dimension        — list name to iterate (default: "platforms")
91	#   env_target       — optional env var name to set to each element per work unit
92	#                      (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2: generic dimension→env mapping declared
93	#                      by the template's `as:` field; empty = no extra env). The
94	#                      strategy is element-name-agnostic — it never hardcodes a var name.
95	#   max_parallel     — concurrency cap (issue #1312): "auto"/empty = CPU-based cap;
96	#                      integer = explicit cap. Enforced via a FIFO-pool batch loop
97	#                      (mirrors ADR-039 parallel_group_run FIFO pool semantics).
98	#   on_member_error  — "collect" (default) or "continue" (issue #1312).
99	#                      continue: a failing element does NOT abort the group (return 0);
100	#                      collect:  any failure is propagated (return 1/2).
101	#                      Unknown values are NOT validated — they fall through to collect
102	#                      (the conservative default), matching parallel_group_run which
103	#                      also silently defaults unknown values to its safe branch.
104	#                      Mirrors parallel_group_run on_member_error semantics (ADR-039).
105	#
106	# Dispatches one work unit per role×element pair.
107	# When dimension=platforms, behavior is byte-identical to _strategy_run_fanout.
108	#
109	# Returns:
110	#   0 — all succeeded, OR on_member_error=continue (even with failures)
111	#   1 — all failed (only when on_member_error=collect)
112	#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail; only when on_member_error=collect)
113	#   3 — empty dimension (no elements to iterate; caller/runner maps to no-op 0)
114	#   4 — no plugin found for any role
115	#   5 — invalid/unknown dimension name (fail-closed; runner surfaces as failure)
116	#   6 — infrastructure failure (orch_spawn failed for a batch sub-pool). Fail-closed:
117	#       NOT subject to on_member_error — an infra failure is never a member outcome.
118	#   Two members that would run under one unit name (#1706) are refused before
119	#   any member starts: rc 1 (ADR-054 §4 — rc says only "failed"); the
120	#   strategy.unit_name_conflict event says why. Not subject to on_member_error.
121	# _map_unit_element <var> <role_count> <role> <element> — sets <var> to the part
122	# of a member's unit name after the stage (#1706): the element, or
123	# <role>.<element> when the map runs more than one role. No subshell per member.
124	_map_unit_element() {
125	    if [[ "$2" -gt 1 ]]; then printf -v "$1" '%s.%s' "$3" "$4"; else printf -v "$1" '%s' "$4"; fi
126	}
127	
128	_strategy_run_map() {
129	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
130	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
131	    # | infra_failed | failed.
132	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
133	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
134	    local dimension="${6:-platforms}" env_target="${7:-}"
135	    local max_raw="${8:-}" on_member_error="${9:-collect}"
136	    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false
137	
138	    # Resolve the iteration list. Capture output AND rc explicitly — a process
139	    # substitution would discard the resolver's status, collapsing an invalid
140	    # dimension (rc=2) into the empty path (rc=3) and masking a fail-closed error.
141	    local _resolved _res_rc
142	    _resolved="$(_strategy_map_resolve_dimension "$dimension")"; _res_rc=$?
143	    if [[ $_res_rc -ne 0 ]]; then
144	        # Invalid/unknown dimension name — fail closed. Distinct from empty (rc=3);
145	        # the runner does NOT map rc=5 to 0, so this surfaces as a real failure.
146	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
147	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="bad_dimension"
148	        return 1
149	    fi
150	
151	    local -a elements=()
152	    local _elem
153	    while IFS= read -r _elem; do
154	        [[ -n "$_elem" ]] && elements+=("$_elem")
155	    done <<< "$_resolved"
156	
157	    if [[ ${#elements[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
158	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
159	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="empty"
160	        return 0
161	    fi
162	
163	    # #1312: resolve the concurrency cap (mirrors ADR-039 FIFO pool).
164	    local max_parallel
165	    max_parallel="$(_strategy_map_resolve_max "$max_raw")"
166	
167	    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): every member runs under <stage>.<element>. Two
168	    # members with one name would write the same records at the same time, so
169	    # the group is refused before any member starts.
170	    # With more than one role every role runs on every element, so the role is
171	    # part of the name: <stage>.<role>.<element>.
172	    local -A _unit_seen=()
173	    local _u_role _u_elem _u_name _u_roles=0
174	    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do [[ -n "$_u_role" ]] && _u_roles=$((_u_roles + 1)); done <<< "$roles_out"
175	    while IFS= read -r _u_role; do
176	        [[ -z "$_u_role" ]] && continue
177	        for _u_elem in "${elements[@]}"; do
178	            _map_unit_element _u_name "$_u_roles" "$_u_role" "$_u_elem"; _u_name="${stage}.${_u_name}"
179	            if [[ -n "${_unit_seen[$_u_name]:-}" ]]; then
180	                warn "map: two members of '$stage' would both run as '$_u_name' — refusing the group" || true
181	                eb_emit_event "strategy.unit_name_conflict" "stage=$stage" "unit=$_u_name" 2>/dev/null || true
182	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
183	                return 1
184	            fi
185	            _unit_seen[$_u_name]=1
186	        done
187	    done <<< "$roles_out"
188	
189	    # Build the ordered list of (plugin_dir, element) work items by iterating
190	    # roles × elements — same order as before, just collected before dispatch.
191	    local -a wu_list=() plugin_list=()
192	    local role element plugin_dir wu
193	    while IFS= read -r role; do
194	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
195	        for element in "${elements[@]}"; do
196	            # Mirror fanout.sh platform-specific then generic resolution.
197	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$element" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
198	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
199	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
200	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
201	            any_plugin_found=true
202	
203	            # Only the platforms dimension populates ZBUILD_PLATFORM (ADR-009 §6
204	            # env contract) — pass the element as the 4th arg so the platforms
205	            # path stays byte-identical to fanout. For non-platform dimensions
206	            # (lenses/mutants), pass the generic element identity via args 5+6
207	            # (ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT / ZBUILD_MAP_DIMENSION, issue #1295, ADR-047 §2)
208	            # so each work unit is distinguishable without hijacking ZBUILD_PLATFORM.
209	            # An optional env_target (arg 7, from the template's `as:`) additionally
210	            # sets a named env var to the element — a generic mapping the strategy
211	            # applies without knowing which dimension or var it is.
212	            _map_unit_element _u_elem "$_u_roles" "$role" "$element"
213	            if [[ "$dimension" == "platforms" ]]; then
214	                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$element" "" "" "" "$_u_elem")"
215	            else
216	                wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "generic" "$element" "$dimension" "$env_target" "$_u_elem")"
217	            fi || {
218	                warn "map: failed to create work unit for role=$role element=$element" || true
219	                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
220	                continue
221	            }
222	            wu_list+=("$wu")
223	            plugin_list+=("$plugin_dir")
224	        done
225	    done <<< "$roles_out"
226	
227	    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
228	        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
229	        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
230	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
231	        return 1
232	    fi
233	
234	    # #1312: FIFO-pool batch dispatch — respects max_parallel cap (ADR-039 model).
235	    # Dispatch up to max_parallel work units per batch; collect before advancing.
236	    # This enforces the concurrency cap via the orch backend's own pool machinery.
237	    # Each batch uses a sub-pool so collect drains only the in-flight batch.
238	    # on_member_error=continue: all batches run regardless of prior batch failures.
239	    local total_wu="${#wu_list[@]}"
240	    local batch_start=0 batch_seq=0
241	    local infra_failed=false   # #1312: orch_spawn failure = infra error → fail-closed
242	    local -a batch_plugins=()
243	    # #1312 (Copilot): backends validate pool_id against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$.
244	    # The per-batch "-b<N>" suffix must not push the id past 64 chars, or orch_spawn
245	    # fails and the whole batch is silently skipped. Keep the base ≤54 chars so
246	    # "<base>-b<N>" always fits (reserve 10 for the largest realistic suffix, e.g.
247	    # "-b99999999").
248	    #
249	    # #1312 (Copilot): collision-safe truncation. Real pool_ids put their UNIQUE
250	    # tail last ("map-<gid>-$$", "zbuild-<stage>-$$-<ns>"), so a plain prefix
251	    # truncation would drop exactly the disambiguating suffix — two distinct bases
252	    # sharing a 54-char prefix would collide into the same sub-pool dir. Instead,
253	    # when over-long, keep a readable 45-char prefix + an 8-char hash of the FULL
254	    # pool_id (45 + 1 + 8 = 54), so distinct bases yield distinct sub-pool bases.
255	    local _sub_pool_base="$pool_id"
256	    if [[ ${#_sub_pool_base} -gt 54 ]]; then
257	        local _pid_hash
258	        _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-8)"
259	        # Fallback if shasum is unavailable: cksum (POSIX) → hex-ish digits.
260	        [[ -n "$_pid_hash" ]] || _pid_hash="$(printf '%s' "$pool_id" | cksum | cut -c1-8)"
261	        _sub_pool_base="${pool_id:0:45}-${_pid_hash}"
262	    fi
263	    while [[ $batch_start -lt $total_wu ]]; do
264	        batch_seq=$(( batch_seq + 1 ))
265	        local sub_pool_id="${_sub_pool_base}-b${batch_seq}"
266	
267	        # #1312 (Copilot): orch_spawn failure is an INFRASTRUCTURE failure, NOT a
268	        # member failure — silently skipping a batch's work units (and possibly
269	        # still returning 0 under on_member_error=continue) hides real breakage.
270	        # Fail closed: stop dispatching and propagate a non-zero rc regardless of
271	        # on_member_error.
272	        if ! orch_spawn "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null; then
273	            warn "map: orch_spawn failed for sub-pool ${sub_pool_id} (infra failure — aborting)" || true
274	            infra_failed=true
275	            break
276	        fi
277	
278	        batch_plugins=()
279	        # #1312 (Copilot): advance batch_start to the next UNPROCESSED index (i),
280	        # NOT by a fixed max_parallel stride. When orch_dispatch fails, batch_dispatched
281	        # does not increment, so the inner loop consumes more than max_parallel indices;
282	        # a fixed stride would then re-process or skip units. `batch_start=i` after the
283	        # loop guarantees every unit is dispatched exactly once.
284	        local batch_dispatched=0 i
285	        for (( i = batch_start; i < total_wu && batch_dispatched < max_parallel; i++ )); do
286	            wu="${wu_list[$i]}"
287	            orch_dispatch "$sub_pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
288	                warn "map: orch_dispatch failed for work unit at index $i" || true
289	                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
290	                continue
291	            }
292	            batch_dispatched=$(( batch_dispatched + 1 ))
293	            batch_plugins+=("${plugin_list[$i]}")
294	        done
295	        batch_start=$i
296	
297	        if [[ $batch_dispatched -gt 0 ]]; then
298	            local collect_rc=0
299	            _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""
300	            orch_collect "$sub_pool_id" || collect_rc=$?
301	
302	            if [[ $collect_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
303	                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
304	                # #1906: artifact enforcement already ran per work unit inside
305	                # plugin_hook_call (scan_plugin_outputs).
306	            elif [[ "${_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME:-}" == "partial" ]]; then
307	                success_count=$(( success_count + 1 ))
308	                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
309	            else
310	                fail_count=$(( fail_count + 1 ))
311	            fi
312	        fi
313	
314	        orch_shutdown "$sub_pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
315	    done
316	
317	    _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${wu_list[@]+"${wu_list[@]}"}"
318	    # Shut down the original pool_id (caller spawned it; we use sub-pools per batch
319	    # but the caller's pool must still be closed via orch_shutdown for contract compliance).
320	    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
321	
322	    # #1312 (Copilot): infra failure (orch_spawn) fails closed — non-zero rc, NOT
323	    # subject to on_member_error. rc=6 is distinct from member outcomes (0/1/2) so
324	    # the runner surfaces it as a real failure even under on_member_error=continue.
325	    if $infra_failed; then
326	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="infra_failed"
327	        return 1
328	    fi
329	
330	    # #1312: on_member_error=collect (default) — propagate failure outward (group
331	    # fails if any element failed). runner.sh's strategy: map/map:* call sites rely
332	    # on this default. on_member_error=continue mirrors parallel_group_run: all
333	    # elements run regardless of failures; group returns 0 even on partial/all-fail.
334	    #
335	    # #1312 (Copilot): unknown on_member_error values are NOT validated — they fall
336	    # through to the collect branch below (the more CONSERVATIVE default). This
337	    # matches parallel_group_run, which also does not validate: it only special-cases
338	    # its recognised enum (`== "collect"`) and treats anything else as its own safe
339	    # default (parallel-orchestrator.sh:317). Neither path fails loud on a typo. Map
340	    # deliberately picks collect (not continue) as the fall-through so a typo cannot
341	    # accidentally make a group non-blocking — safer to over-report than to swallow
342	    # a failure. (parallel defaults empty→continue; map defaults empty→collect per
343	    # its strategy: call-site contract, but both fall through to their safe default.)
344	    if [[ "$on_member_error" == "continue" ]]; then
345	        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
346	        return 0
347	    fi
348	
349	    if   [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]];    then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"; return 0
350	    elif [[ $success_count -gt 0 ]]; then _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="partial"; return 1
351	    else                                  _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"; return 1
352	    fi
353	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh — serialized per-platform dispatch (issue #200/#222)
3	# ADR-009: platforms run one at a time; always halts on the first collect failure.
4	# Depends on core/orch/contract.sh being sourced first by the caller (runner.sh).
5	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
6	
7	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
8	_ZBUILD_STRATEGY_SEQUENTIAL_LOADED=1
9	
10	_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	source "${_ZBUILD_STRATEGIES_DIR_SEQ}/common.sh"
12	
13	# ─── _strategy_run_sequential ────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	# Usage: _strategy_run_sequential <pool_id> <stage> <roles_out> <state_file> <plugins_root>
15	#   pool_id    — caller-supplied, already validated
16	#   stage      — stage name
17	#   roles_out  — newline-delimited list of role names
18	#   state_file — path to pipeline state file
19	#   plugins_root — path to plugins directory
20	#
21	# Dispatches one work unit at a time via orch_dispatch + orch_collect.
22	# Halts on first failure (does not continue to next platform/role).
23	# Always calls orch_shutdown on exit (success or failure).
24	# Artifact enforcement happens per work unit inside plugin_hook_call (#1906).
25	#
26	# Returns:
27	#   0 — all succeeded
28	#   1 — any collect/dispatch failure
29	#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
30	_strategy_run_sequential() {
31	    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
32	    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
33	    # | infra_failed | failed.
34	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
35	    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
36	    local any_plugin_found=false
37	
38	    local role platform plugin_dir wu prc
39	    while IFS= read -r role; do
40	        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
41	        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
42	            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
43	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
44	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
45	            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
46	            any_plugin_found=true
47	
48	            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
49	                warn "sequential: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
50	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
51	                return 1
52	            }
53	
54	            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
55	                warn "sequential: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
56	                rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
57	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
58	                return 1
59	            }
60	
61	            prc=0
62	            orch_collect "$pool_id" || prc=$?
63	            rm -f "$wu" 2>/dev/null || true
64	
65	            if [[ $prc -ne 0 ]]; then
66	                warn "sequential: stage=$stage role=$role platform=$platform failed (rc=$prc)" || true
67	                orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
68	                return 1
69	            fi
70	
71	        done
72	    done <<< "$roles_out"
73	
74	    orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
75	    $any_plugin_found || { _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"; return 1; }
76	    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="ok"
77	    return 0
78	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/pipeline/template.sh — Template loading and stage resolution (issue #208)
3	# ADR-009 (platform-aware modularity), ADR-013 (canonical stage sequence)
4	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
5	
6	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
7	_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_LOADED=1
8	
9	_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
10	_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "$_ZBUILD_TEMPLATE_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
11	
12	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
13	source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
14	# shellcheck source=../plugin-registry/registry.sh
15	source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh"
16	# ADR-027 (Wave 17-B #703): template.deprecated_shape event on old-shape load.
17	# Defensive source — event-bus is a no-op when ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL is unset.
18	if ! declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
19	    # shellcheck source=../event-bus/event-bus.sh
20	    source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
21	fi
22	
23	# ADR-047 §5 (#1299): stage membership + order are NOT an engine-owned hardcoded
24	# roster. Membership is enforced by the manifest-derived resolvability preflight
25	# (_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability, runner.sh — every leaf must resolve to a
26	# plugin) and order by the upstream-input data-dependency DAG (contract-validator.sh).
27	# The retired _ZBUILD_CANONICAL_STAGES array + ZBUILD_LEGACY_STAGE_VALIDATION
28	# kill-switch (the strangler escape hatch) are deleted; the preflight + DAG are the
29	# sole enforcement.
30	
31	# Module-level state — populated by load_template
32	_TPL_DEFAULT_STRATEGY="fanout"
33	_TPL_MERGE_POLICY="auto_unless_flagged"
34	_TPL_STAGES=()
35	# #1831: ordered stage ids that run on EVERY exit path (success, non-zero rc,
36	# SIGINT, SIGTERM, timeout). Declared by the template's top-level `always_run:`
37	# list, NOT part of _TPL_STAGES[] — an always-run stage is not in the flow.
38	_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN=()
39	# ADR-021 (#512): list of dispatch units in template order. Each entry is
40	# "stage:<id>" or "cycle:<id>". Empty `cycles:` block → every unit is "stage:<id>"
41	# (backwards-compat — runner behavior identical to today).
42	_TPL_DISPATCH_UNITS=()
43	# ADR-021: list of cycle ids declared in template (in declaration order).
44	_TPL_CYCLES=()
45	# ADR-039 (#1130): list of parallel group ids declared in template (in
46	# declaration order). Sibling of _TPL_CYCLES — a `type: parallel` group folds
47	# to one "parallel:<gid>" dispatch unit. Template-layer parse/validate only;
48	# execution lands in a later issue.
49	_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS=()
50	# issue #1295 (ADR-047 §2): list of map group ids declared in template (in
51	# declaration order). A `type: map` group folds to one "map:<gid>" dispatch unit.
52	_TPL_MAP_GROUPS=()
53	
54	# ADR-015 v1 (#438): recognized io.destination tokens. Unknown tokens fail at
55	# template load time with an actionable error listing the valid set.
56	readonly _ZBUILD_IO_DESTINATIONS_VALID=(file stdout gh_comment)
57	
58	load_template() {
59	    local template_file="$1"
60	    if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
61	        error "load_template: file not found: $template_file"
62	        return 1
63	    fi
64	    # ADR-036 #1188: remember the source path so lightweight per-stage getters
65	    # (e.g. template_stage_negctl_timeout) can read additive scalar knobs without
66	    # threading them through the pipe-delimited row shape.
67	    _TPL_SOURCE_FILE="$template_file"; export _TPL_SOURCE_FILE
68	
69	    # ADR-021 v2 (#585): legacy top-level `cycles:` block is a hard-break.
70	    # Detect and refuse with a pointer to the migration helper.
71	    if awk 'BEGIN{rc=1} /^cycles:[[:space:]]*$/ {rc=0; exit} END{exit rc}' "$template_file"; then
72	        error "load_template: legacy 'cycles:' block detected in $template_file"
73	        error "  v2 template syntax inlines cycles as stage entries (type: cycle)"
74	        error "  with per-stage attributes hoisted into a top-level"
75	        error "  'stage_definitions:' map (see ADR-021 v2 / issue #585)."
76	        error "  Run: scripts/migrate-template-v2.sh '$template_file' --in-place"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
3	#
4	# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
5	# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
6	# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
7	#
8	#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
9	#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
10	#
11	# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
12	# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
13	# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
14	#
15	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.
16	
17	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
18	_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1
19	
20	# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
21	# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
22	# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
23	# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
24	if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
25	   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
26	   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
27	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
28	else
29	    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
30	fi
31	
32	_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
33	_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
34	
35	# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
36	# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
37	# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
38	# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
39	# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
40	# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
41	# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)
42	
43	# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
44	# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
45	_orch_not_implemented() {
46	    local fn_name="$1"
47	    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
48	    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
49	    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
51	    fi
52	    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
53	    return 1
54	}
55	
56	# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
57	# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.
58	
59	if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
61	fi
62	
63	if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
64	    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
65	fi
66	
67	if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
68	    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
69	    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
70	    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
71	    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
72	    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
73	fi
74	
75	if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
76	    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
77	fi
78	
79	if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
80	    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
81	fi
82	
83	# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
84	# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
85	# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
86	# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
87	orch_has_capability() {
88	    local cap="$1"
89	    local caps
90	    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
91	    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then

95	}
96	
97	# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
98	# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
99	# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
100	#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
101	#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
102	# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
103	_orch_find_backend_dir() {
104	    local alias="$1"
105	    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"
106	
107	    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1
108	
109	    local manifest plugin_dir
110	    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
111	        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
112	        # Check provides.role
113	        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
114	            continue
115	        fi
116	        # Check id or provides.alias match
117	        local id declared_alias
118	        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
119	        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
120	        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
121	            echo "$plugin_dir"
122	            return 0
123	        fi
124	    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)
125	
126	    return 1
127	}
128	
129	# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
130	# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
131	# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
132	# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
133	# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
134	# Missing or unreadable backend is misconfigured (no fallback).
135	# If no plugin is found, emits orch.backend.misconfigured and returns 1.
136	orch_load_backend() {
137	    local backend="${1:-}"
138	    local plugin_dir
139	
140	    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
141	        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	
145	    # "sequential" and the long-form alias are retired — emit misconfigured immediately.
146	    # (Build the retired long-form by concatenation so no stale literal appears here.)
147	    local _retired_long="orch-"
148	    _retired_long+="sequential"
149	    if [[ "$backend" == "sequential" || "$backend" == "$_retired_long" ]]; then
150	        if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
151	            emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
152	                "reason=sequential backends retired; use bash-parallel" || true
153	        fi
154	        warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' is misconfigured — sequential backends are retired; configure bash-parallel instead" || true
155	        return 1
156	    fi
157	
158	    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
159	    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
161	        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
162	            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
163	            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
164	            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
165	            return 0
166	        fi
167	    fi
168	
169	    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
170	    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
171	    # When ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is set to a directory other than the engine's own
172	    # plugins (e.g. a test temp dir), also search the engine's plugins so that
173	    # backends like bash-parallel remain resolvable without installing them there.
174	    if [[ -z "$plugin_dir" || ! -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
175	        local _engine_plugins="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins"
176	        if [[ "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-}" != "" && \
177	              "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT}" != "${_engine_plugins}" ]]; then
178	            plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" "${_engine_plugins}" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
179	        fi
180	    fi
181	    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
182	        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
183	        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
184	        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
185	        return 0
186	    fi
187	
188	    # Backend not found — misconfigured, not a silent fallback.
189	    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
190	        emit_event "orch.backend.misconfigured" "backend=$backend" \
191	            "reason=no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias $backend" || true
192	    fi
193	    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' misconfigured — not found (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias ${backend})" || true

195	}
196	
197	# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
198	# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
199	# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
200	# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
201	_orch_load_backend() {
202	    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
203	    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
204	    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
205	    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
206	    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0
207	
208	    local backend
209	
210	    # Get configured backend, falling back to "bash-parallel" if config unavailable
211	    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
212	        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="bash-parallel"
213	    else
214	        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-bash-parallel}"
215	    fi
216	
217	    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
218	    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
219	    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
220	}
221	
222	# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
223	_orch_load_backend

Perfect! I've successfully read all the requested files. Here's a comprehensive compilation of the key files for the per-dispatch stage timeout design (issue #1801):

## Design.md (Previous Notes Summary)

The design notes confirm three failing tests with root causes identified:

**1. stage-timeout-dispatch-test.sh SPEC-10**: Line 525 in lifecycle.sh uses `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid"` which tests grep for. Fix: replace with `zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true`

**2. runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh SPEC-6b**: Outer watchdog kills plugin_hook_call process via TERM, bash exits on TERM (no trap), and the inner hook group is orphaned. Fix: Add TERM trap inside the run-hook branch of plugin_hook_call that kills _lc_hook_pid group before exiting.

**3. runner-job-control-abort-test.sh T1 flag-on**: Plugin subshell has `set +m`, but test expects to see m flag. Fix: Update T1 assertion to structural check.

---

## lifecycle.sh (Plugin Hook Dispatch - Core File)

**Key Function: plugin_hook_call (lines 185-630)**

The "run" hook dispatch with per-dispatch timeout (lines 485-533):

```bash
if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
    # Load zbuild_pg_kill if needed
    if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    
    # Build timeout variable name from stage name
    local _lc_stage_safe="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE//-/_}"
    local _lc_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_${_lc_stage_safe}"
    local _lc_hook_to="${!_lc_to_var:-}"
    
    # Precedence: template override > env var > default 5400s
    [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to="${ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S:-5400}"
    [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to=5400
    
    local _lc_hook_pid _lc_wd_pid _lc_m_before=0
    [[ "$-" == *m* ]] && _lc_m_before=1
    set -m  # Enable job control
    
    (
        set +m  # Run hook in no-monitor mode
        source "$plugin_sh"
        if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            "$hook_fn" "$@"
        else
            echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    ) &
    _lc_hook_pid=$!
    
    # Arm inner watchdog: TERM after timeout_s, then KILL after 10s grace
    ( set +m; sleep "$_lc_hook_to"; zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _lc_wd_pid=$!
    
    set +m  # Restore monitor mode
    (( _lc_m_before == 1 )) && set -m  # If caller had it, restore
    
    wait "$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
    
    # Kill any survivors (group leader exit doesn't guarantee group is dead)
    kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Clean up the watchdog
    declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1 && zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_wd_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_lc_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Check if timeout occurred
    if (( rc == 143 || rc == 137 )); then
        emit_event "plugin.run.timed_out" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" \
            "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "timeout_s=${_lc_hook_to}" \
            "disposition=timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
```

**Critical Design Points:**
- **Timeout source hierarchy**: Template-specific override (`_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>`) > global env (`ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S`) > hardcoded default (5400s)
- **Two-level timeout control**: Outer watchdog fires at `timeout_s`, then inner watchdog completes with KILL after 10s grace
- **Job control isolation**: `set +m` inside plugin subshell ensures child processes don't escape the KILL signal
- **Monitor mode restoration**: Captures pre-call state, restores it after to prevent interference with caller

---

## proc-group.sh (Process Group Kill Helpers)

**Key Functions:**

**zbuild_pg_resolve (lines 28-50)**: Safely resolves a PGID, returns nothing if it would signal the runner's own group.

**zbuild_pg_kill (lines 146-154)**: TERM then KILL a process group after grace period. Refuses to signal the runner's own group.

**zbuild_pid_kill (lines 159-163)**: Same escalation for a single PID (fallback when no group could be proven).

**_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill (lines 61-73)**: Core escalation: TERM, poll for grace_s seconds, then KILL.

---

## runner.sh (Dispatch Orchestration)

**Key points from first 1227 lines:**
- Runner-level helpers for artifact snapshots, stage timing, and pipeline status
- `_runner_snapshot_artifacts` (line 332): Snapshots at each stage boundary (Advisory, never fatal)
- `_runner_duration_token` (line 511): Formats elapsed time for operator display
- `_runner_now_ms` (line 421): Millisecond wall clock for duration measurement

---

## local_engine.sh (Orchestrator Dispatch/Collect)

**_orch_local_dispatch_workunit (lines 51-92)**: Spawns work unit in background subshell with inner/outer PID tracking.

**_orch_local_collect_results (lines 103-160)**: **Important for timeout enforcement:**
- Polls `.exit` files for work-unit completion
- **Timeout handling (lines 125-134)**: If timeout_s is exceeded, kills the wrapper and inner PID, writes exit code 124 (timeout)
- Calls `zbuild_pg_kill` for graceful termination or falls back to `kill -TERM`

---

## Strategy Files (fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh)

All three use the same dispatch pattern via `_strategy_make_work_unit` (in common.sh) and `orch_dispatch`/`orch_collect`. The per-dispatch timeout is applied at the **plugin_hook_call level**, not at the strategy level.

---

## contract.sh (Orchestrator Contract)

Defines the 5 backend contract functions:
- `orch_spawn` — prepare a pool
- `orch_dispatch` — send work to the pool
- `orch_collect` — wait for all results (with timeout support)
- `orch_shutdown` — tear down the pool
- `orch_capabilities` — report backend capabilities

The timeout_s parameter flows from runner → strategy → orch_collect → local_engine poll loop.

---

## Summary

**Issue #1801 per-dispatch stage timeout design:**

1. **Configuration source hierarchy**: `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>` (template) → `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` (env) → 5400s (default)

2. **Execution model** in `plugin_hook_call`:
   - Outer watchdog (inner zbuild_pg_kill call) sends TERM after timeout_s
   - Inner watchdog arm sends KILL after 10s grace

Perfect! I've successfully read all the requested files. Here's a comprehensive compilation of the key files for the per-dispatch stage timeout design (issue #1801):

## Design.md (Previous Notes Summary)

The design notes confirm three failing tests with root causes identified:

**1. stage-timeout-dispatch-test.sh SPEC-10**: Line 525 in lifecycle.sh uses `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid"` which tests grep for. Fix: replace with `zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true`

**2. runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh SPEC-6b**: Outer watchdog kills plugin_hook_call process via TERM, bash exits on TERM (no trap), and the inner hook group is orphaned. Fix: Add TERM trap inside the run-hook branch of plugin_hook_call that kills _lc_hook_pid group before exiting.

**3. runner-job-control-abort-test.sh T1 flag-on**: Plugin subshell has `set +m`, but test expects to see m flag. Fix: Update T1 assertion to structural check.

---

## lifecycle.sh (Plugin Hook Dispatch - Core File)

**Key Function: plugin_hook_call (lines 185-630)**

The "run" hook dispatch with per-dispatch timeout (lines 485-533):

```bash
if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
    # Load zbuild_pg_kill if needed
    if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    
    # Build timeout variable name from stage name
    local _lc_stage_safe="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE//-/_}"
    local _lc_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_${_lc_stage_safe}"
    local _lc_hook_to="${!_lc_to_var:-}"
    
    # Precedence: template override > env var > default 5400s
    [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to="${ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S:-5400}"
    [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to=5400
    
    local _lc_hook_pid _lc_wd_pid _lc_m_before=0
    [[ "$-" == *m* ]] && _lc_m_before=1
    set -m  # Enable job control
    
    (
        set +m  # Run hook in no-monitor mode
        source "$plugin_sh"
        if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            "$hook_fn" "$@"
        else
            echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    ) &
    _lc_hook_pid=$!
    
    # Arm inner watchdog: TERM after timeout_s, then KILL after 10s grace
    ( set +m; sleep "$_lc_hook_to"; zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _lc_wd_pid=$!
    
    set +m  # Restore monitor mode
    (( _lc_m_before == 1 )) && set -m  # If caller had it, restore
    
    wait "$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
    
    # Kill any survivors (group leader exit doesn't guarantee group is dead)
    kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Clean up the watchdog
    declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1 && zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_wd_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_lc_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    
    # Check if timeout occurred
    if (( rc == 143 || rc == 137 )); then
        emit_event "plugin.run.timed_out" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" \
            "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "timeout_s=${_lc_hook_to}" \
            "disposition=timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
```

**Critical Design Points:**
- **Timeout source hierarchy**: Template-specific override (`_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>`) > global env (`ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S`) > hardcoded default (5400s)
- **Two-level timeout control**: Outer watchdog fires at `timeout_s`, then inner watchdog completes with KILL after 10s grace
- **Job control isolation**: `set +m` inside plugin subshell ensures child processes don't escape the KILL signal
- **Monitor mode restoration**: Captures pre-call state, restores it after to prevent interference with caller

---

## proc-group.sh (Process Group Kill Helpers)

**Key Functions:**

**zbuild_pg_resolve (lines 28-50)**: Safely resolves a PGID, returns nothing if it would signal the runner's own group.

**zbuild_pg_kill (lines 146-154)**: TERM then KILL a process group after grace period. Refuses to signal the runner's own group.

**zbuild_pid_kill (lines 159-163)**: Same escalation for a single PID (fallback when no group could be proven).

**_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill (lines 61-73)**: Core escalation: TERM, poll for grace_s seconds, then KILL.

---

## runner.sh (Dispatch Orchestration)

**Key points from first 1227 lines:**
- Runner-level helpers for artifact snapshots, stage timing, and pipeline status
- `_runner_snapshot_artifacts` (line 332): Snapshots at each stage boundary (Advisory, never fatal)
- `_runner_duration_token` (line 511): Formats elapsed time for operator display
- `_runner_now_ms` (line 421): Millisecond wall clock for duration measurement

---

## local_engine.sh (Orchestrator Dispatch/Collect)

**_orch_local_dispatch_workunit (lines 51-92)**: Spawns work unit in background subshell with inner/outer PID tracking.

**_orch_local_collect_results (lines 103-160)**: **Important for timeout enforcement:**
- Polls `.exit` files for work-unit completion
- **Timeout handling (lines 125-134)**: If timeout_s is exceeded, kills the wrapper and inner PID, writes exit code 124 (timeout)
- Calls `zbuild_pg_kill` for graceful termination or falls back to `kill -TERM`

---

## Strategy Files (fanout.sh, sequential.sh, map.sh)

All three use the same dispatch pattern via `_strategy_make_work_unit` (in common.sh) and `orch_dispatch`/`orch_collect`. The per-dispatch timeout is applied at the **plugin_hook_call level**, not at the strategy level.

---

## contract.sh (Orchestrator Contract)

Defines the 5 backend contract functions:
- `orch_spawn` — prepare a pool
- `orch_dispatch` — send work to the pool
- `orch_collect` — wait for all results (with timeout support)
- `orch_shutdown` — tear down the pool
- `orch_capabilities` — report backend capabilities

The timeout_s parameter flows from runner → strategy → orch_collect → local_engine poll loop.

---

## Summary

**Issue #1801 per-dispatch stage timeout design:**

1. **Configuration source hierarchy**: `_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage>` (template) → `ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S` (env) → 5400s (default)

2. **Execution model** in `plugin_hook_call`:
   - Outer watchdog (inner zbuild_pg_kill call) sends TERM after timeout_s
   - Inner watchdog arm sends KILL after 10s grace
   - Job control (`set -m` / `set +m`) ensures signals reach all descendants

3. **Test fixes required**:
   - Replace `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid"` with `zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 1`
   - Add TERM trap in run-hook branch to kill inner group on outer timeout
   - Update T1 assertion for monitor mode check

# Design notes — issue #1801 (retry)

## Previous notes summary
Previous build ran (39 files changed). Three tests still fail.

## Root causes confirmed

### 1. stage-timeout-dispatch-test.sh SPEC-10
lifecycle.sh line 525: `kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true`
Test greps for kill -KILL / kill -TERM in plugin_hook_call body.
Fix: replace with `zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true`

### 2. runner-release-exit-paths-test.sh SPEC-6b
Outer watchdog in _runner_dispatch_always_run kills `plugin_hook_call` (the _ar_pid
process) via TERM. Bash exits on TERM (no trap). The inner hook group (_lc_hook_pid)
is orphaned. The inner watchdog fires late. Fix: TERM trap inside the run-hook branch
of plugin_hook_call that kills _lc_hook_pid group before exiting.

### 3. runner-job-control-abort-test.sh T1 flag-on
Plugin subshell always has `set +m` now. The T1 probe records $- inside the plugin.
$- never has m. Fix: update T1 assertion to structural check (grep runner.sh/lifecycle.sh).

## SPEC-6b deeper analysis
_runner_dispatch_always_run outer watchdog: zbuild_pg_kill "$_ar_pid" 10
  → TERM to _ar_pid's group (only plugin_hook_call process, since _lc_hook_pid is
    a separate group created by set -m inside plugin_hook_call)
  → plugin_hook_call receives TERM, bash exits (default TERM action)
  → _lc_hook_pid's group orphaned

Inner watchdog: (set +m; sleep 30; zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 10 ...) &
  → still alive (in its own group), fires 30s after dispatch
  → TERM to _lc_hook_pid group, wait 10s, KILL
  → child dies at ~40s after dispatch start

Runner returns at ~30s (after _ar_pid dies). Test polls for 5s (30-35s).
Child alive at 35s → SPEC-6b fails.

Fix: trap TERM in plugin_hook_call run-hook branch:
trap 'zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true; ...' TERM
This kills the inner group immediately when plugin_hook_call receives TERM from the outer watchdog.

## Design document structure
Will produce design.md with all files in scope and SPEC list aligned to R-1..R-13.

32	#    after run completes with exit 0, the engine emits a synthetic blocking
33	#    finding."
34	# #1906 retired provides.artifact_type, which the original wording keyed on;
35	# outputs[].required is the single declaration the scan now honours.

39	#   $2 — state_file (so $state_dir / $artifacts_dir can substitute into paths)
40	#
41	# Returns:
42	#   0 if all declared outputs are present (or no outputs declared).
43	#   1 if any declared output is missing — and emits one
44	#      `plugin.artifact.missing` event per missing path.

608	            fi
609	        fi
610	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.complete" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
611	    else
612	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "rc=$rc"
613	    fi
614	
615	    # #2183: keep THIS attempt's declared outputs before the next dispatch can
616	    # overwrite them. After the rc branches, so a FAILED attempt — the one whose
617	    # record matters most — is archived too. Fail-open by construction.
618	    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_archive_outputs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
619	        attempt_archive_outputs "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "$rc" "$_lc_outputs_before" 2>/dev/null || true
620	    fi
621	
622	    # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): the plugin's raw status passes through UNCHANGED, and
623	    # deliberately so during versioned coexistence. A v1 plugin has no result
624	    # field in which to say what its rc says — `plan`'s rc=10 IS its only way to
625	    # report `scope_too_large` — so narrowing here would destroy the meaning of
626	    # every unmigrated plugin at once. The narrowing is gated on the result
627	    # contract at the dispatch boundary instead (see cycle_dispatch_stage), and
628	    # becomes unconditional in #1850 when the last v1 reader is dropped.
629	    return $rc
630	}
